label: GPON OLT class C+, 8 ports
notes: Class C+ per ITU-T G.984.2 Amendment 2 (03/2008), Appendix V, Table V.1 (2.488 Gbit/s downstream, 1.244 Gbit/s upstream single-sided reach-extended system): OLT mean launched power +3..+7 dBm, OLT receiver minimum sensitivity -32 dBm, OLT receiver minimum overload -12 dBm; ONU launch +0.5..+5 dBm, ONU sensitivity -30 dBm, ONU overload -8 dBm; class C+ ODN is 17..32 dB (Table V.2). The two receiver figures were wrong in this row until 2026-11-24 - it carried -30/-8, which is the class B+ pair, and that made the row contradict its own 32 dB budget: an ONU launching +0.5 dBm into a -30 dBm receiver has 30.5 dB, so a legal 32 dB C+ ODN would have failed the receiver-headroom verdict while passing the class verdict on the same row. At -32 the upstream pair is 0.5 - (-32) = 32.5 dB and the class budget is again the tighter of the two verdicts, as it is on every other OLT row here. Caveat that travels with the sensitivity: Table V.1 NOTE 1 states the -32 dBm assumes the G-PON TC layer's optional RS(255,239) FEC plus intrinsic detector improvements such as SOA preamplification, at a pre-FEC BER of 1e-4 - a line card without FEC is not this row, and the class budget is not reachable without it at 1310 nm. The -12 dBm overload is the reach-extended OLT's own figure, not class B+'s -8: a very short ODN saturates this card 4 dB earlier than a B+ card would, which is the direction that costs a pad, never reach. 1:128 is the split a 32 dB ODN supports, not a standards figure - confirm the card's own limit. Class figures from the recommendation, not one measured card: replace with the line card actually purchased before construction.
